slides.texte_overlay:
things you should stop
apologising for

taking up space

stop saying sorry for sitting down, asking a question or being in the room. you belong there as much as anyone, and apologising for existing teaches people you don't.

having needs

stop apologising for needing rest, help or time alone. everyone has needs, and the people who state theirs calmly are the ones others quietly respect the most.

not knowing everything

stop apologising for what you don't know yet. learning a little every day, like a fact about history or science, is how everyone gets smart, slowly and quietly.
slides.texte_sophia:
not knowing everything

i stopped apologising for what i didn't know. i do it with the Sophia app now, one lesson a day, a fact about history or science, and that's how everyone gets smart, slowly and quietly.

slides.texte_overlay:
changing your mind

stop saying sorry for changing your opinion after learning something new. updating your views is a clear sign of a growing mind, not an unreliable one.

saying no

stop apologising for saying no to things you don't want to do. a calm, kind no protects your time, and the right people in your life will always understand it.
